content:
With the release of the seventh developer betas for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and Apple's other upcoming software updates, Apple is now rolling out the corresponding public betas. Here are the details.

Apple releases new public betas

Apple released the following versions this morning:

  • iOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (build number: 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (build number: 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate Developer Beta 7 (build number: 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (build number: 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (build number: 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (build number: 24R5358a)

Apple is now pushing the corresponding versions to the public beta channel — this marks the fifth round of public beta releases. So far, Apple has rolled out new public betas for iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's releases do not contain any particularly notable new changes, as Apple is currently focused on bug fixes and stability improvements in preparation for the official release expected in a few weeks.

Additionally, shortly after rolling out the corresponding developer Release Candidate (RC) earlier today, Apple has followed up with the second public Release Candidate of macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20). The second RC of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is expected to follow later. This update was made available at 7:42 PM Eastern Time.

Across all of today's releases, the public beta build numbers match those of their corresponding developer versions.

Sign up for the Apple Beta Software Program

To enrol your device in the public beta programme, visit https://beta.apple.com and follow the steps for each respective device. Here's how to install the public beta on your iPhone:

  • Go to the Apple Beta Software Program website and select "Sign Up" or "Sign In".
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone, then accept the programme terms and enrol your account.
  • Open Settings on your iPhone.
  • Go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates.
  • Select "iOS 27 Public Beta".
  • Return to the Software Update screen, then tap "Update Now" when the beta appears.

Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you're using your primary iPhone, be sure to make a recent backup first.

Have you spotted any changes in today's beta? Let us know in the comments.
